fit_notes: Envelope-encrypt-values-in-file pattern (per-file data key encrypted to each master key, MAC stored in the file, per-path creation_rules) fits git-committed, long-lived site secrets, not a per-conversation, short-TTL model-boundary vault (no native TTL; only an optional per-decrypt audit log to PostgreSQL).

BSD-3-Clause permits use as-is; the age format is built on X25519, HKDF-SHA-256 and ChaCha20-Poly1305, primitives a pure-Python re-implementation would take from a library such as `cryptography`, so it is portable into a pure-Python, no-Rust package.

Confirmed by direct LICENSE fetch: Business Source License 1.1 for Vault 1.15.0 and later; it allows copying, modification and non-production use, production use only under the Additional Use Grant (no competing offering), and each version changes to MPL 2.0 after four years. Also requires an always-on Vault server, which conflicts with a no-always-on-service constraint.

Confirmed dual-licensed (Apache-2.0 or BSD-3-Clause) by direct LICENSE fetch. `Fernet.decrypt(token, ttl=seconds)` raises InvalidToken for a token older than ttl seconds, exactly the kind of TTL check a short-lived pseudonymization vault needs, replacing bespoke AEAD+TTL logic.
GPL-3.0: no copying under a permissive, no-GPL policy. Transparent per-file git filter model does not match a runtime vault (per-conversation, TTL, audited reveal) anyway.
A commonly chosen component for PII detection and anonymization pipelines. MIT permits use/copy with notice.

MIT permits copying with notice. Its `Vault` class (placeholder<->value mapping object shared between Anonymize and Deanonymize scanners) is a close structural match for pseudonymization vault objects generally; worth porting the mapping-object shape, not the whole scanner pipeline where a detector is already chosen.

Apache-2.0 permits copying. Format-preserving encryption is a fallback idea only if a token kind needs to keep exact alphabet/length; bespoke partial-preserving rules per token kind (e.g. keeping a subnet or a domain RID) may already cover the need without copying code. Its README notes NIST's February 2025 Draft 2 withdrew FF3 and FF3-1 over published vulnerabilities.

Licence would permit copying, but Puppet's `--noop` runs its own catalog/agent model (Ruby), incompatible with a stack that has already chosen DSC v3 as the declared source of truth for read-only drift checks. Nothing to replace.

Confirmed Apache-2.0 by direct LICENSE fetch (repo metadata reported NOASSERTION). Its read-only, no-enforcement design validates a test-mode-only, remediation-off rollout approach, but it is Ruby, not portable into a pure-Python package.

Resources at release 1.26.909.1 are classic PowerShell DSC modules (Get/Set/Test-TargetResource), not DSC v3 manifests. MIT PowerShell resource code is out of scope for a Python-core tool; relevant only if that tool ever ships its own DSC resources.

Wrong domain (ITSM/service desk) and GPL-3.0 copyleft: copied code would carry GPL terms, which a no-GPL policy excludes. No merge-key/precedence documentation was found to borrow as a pattern either.
Wrong domain (asset/licence tracking) and AGPL-3.0 copyleft: copied code would carry AGPL terms, which a no-GPL policy excludes. No merge-key precedence documentation found.

Licence would permit copying, but NetBox's domain (IPAM/DCIM, network/rack-centric) does not match a device-identity merge problem across multiple id spaces (e.g. Entra deviceId / AD SID / Intune id / ZTDID / serial), and no comparable merge-key algorithm was found documented at the depth fetched.

Core confirmed MIT by direct LICENSE fetch (docs CC BY-SA 4.0, ee/ under its own licence, JS under MIT Expat). Licence would permit copying the MIT core, but Fleet is a device-management system with an agent on devices and a GUI/REST API, an always-on service that conflicts with a no-always-on-service constraint; no Fleet-specific merge-key algorithm was confirmed to add value over hand-specified rules.

Confirms role/ACL-gated execution as an established idea; a small in-process tier-gating scheme (a few dozen lines) is too small a surface to justify importing a full job-execution platform, and Rundeck is an always-on service.
Same reasoning as Rundeck: its rules engine and workflows validate tier gating conceptually; running it would add a new always-on service.

AGPL-3.0 forbids copying. Access Requests (named, mechanics not fetched this session) is a plausible pattern for future approval workflows, but not reusable as code and not needed for a small, already-designed tier scheme.

Confirmed Apache-2.0 by direct LICENSE fetch. Licence permits copying, but AWX is a full web+API+task-engine service; running or importing it adds infrastructure a no-always-on-service, Python-package-only constraint forbids. RBAC/workflow-approval concept only (pattern).

Confirmed: catalog lists only Azure.Mcp.Server, Fabric.Mcp.Server, Template.Mcp.Server at the fetched commit -- no ConfigMgr/Intune/Graph-device/Entra server exists to reuse. Nothing to import; a custom MCP tool surface for these APIs stays custom.

Licence permits copying, but it is an executable that runs as an agent daemon or gateway; no built-in CMTrace parser was found. An inline fetch/normalize library step is a better fit than a piped collector.

Same reasoning as OTel Collector: a telemetry agent (always-on service model) conflicts with a no-service constraint; supports Windows but no built-in CMTrace parser found; not a fit for an inline normalize step.

Implements a common settings precedence (flags > env vars > config file > defaults) via its documented source priority and the `settings_customise_sources` hook. Unknown-key refusal is partial: the default extra='forbid' rejects unmatched dotenv entries, but env vars matching no field are ignored, so env-var refusal and a nearest-key-name message need custom code. Shrinks the settings-resolution slice of a custom implementation considerably.

MIT permits use, but its README does not document unknown-key refusal (a commonly stated requirement), and it adds provider surface (Vault, Redis) that is not needed -- a new store/dependency that a simplicity-first design argues against when pydantic-settings alone already meets the spec.
